dedupe_keys.name: riksantikvaren building heritage data for norway protected buildings and the sefrak register of pre 1900 buildings

description: Riksantikvaren, Norway's Directorate for Cultural Heritage, publishes two national building datasets from its Askeladden heritage database on Geonorge. Freda bygninger holds buildings and churches protected under the Cultural Heritage Act, whether automatically (buildings older than 1537, Sami buildings over 100 years old), by decision, by regulation for state buildings or temporarily, plus listed churches; it is updated weekly. SEFRAK is a national register of older buildings and other heritage sites, in which all buildings from before 1900 were recorded, and in Finnmark up to 1945; it gives no protection status by itself. Coverage: all of Norway; Kulturminnesøk, the public search site built on Askeladden, holds over 220,000 heritage objects of all kinds. Access: free downloads as national, county or municipal files in FGDB, GML, PostGIS and SOSI. Licence: NLOD, but the metadata says Askeladden data may not be resold and written permission is needed before inclusion in products or redistribution; free. Caveats: the metadata warns that quality is uneven and that detailed planning should involve regional heritage authorities; the protected buildings product is marked as under work. Simulation uses are heritage building locations and ages for hazard exposure and adaptation planning. Related records: the Matrikkelen building points (which carry SEFRAK ids) and the Irish NIAH inventory.
licence: NLOD (Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data), with Riksantikvaren conditions on resale and redistribution
